Erdős problem #257

Reciprocal sums over infinite exponent supports

Is the sum of 1/(2𝑛 −1)1/(2n−1) over every infinite set of positive exponents irrational?

Open Problem on GitHub
Read the short paperPDFOpen the PDF, 26 pagesLean map
Results189/388 examplePapersLean source filesWhat is checked

Results and open questions

#257. Fix a finite nonempty set of primes 𝑃P and let ℎ(𝑎)h(a) be the largest divisor of 𝑎a supported on 𝑃P. For an infinite support 𝐴A and an integer base 𝑏 ≥2b≥2, finiteness of ∑𝑎∈𝐴ℎ(𝑎)/(𝑎(𝑏ℎ(𝑎) −1))∑a∈Ah(a)/(a(bh(a)−1)) implies irrationality of ∑𝑎∈𝐴1/(𝑏𝑎 −1)∑a∈A1/(ba−1). The long paper explains the proof: if this sum were rational with denominator 𝑣v, every positive displacement from an integer would be at least 1/𝑣1/v. Choose a finite part of 𝐴A and make its exponents divide an observation modulus 𝑄Q, so their displacements vanish.

For the remaining exponents, a complete residue orbit gives the weighted main term. Averaging over a finite block of dyadic observation lengths charges the incomplete orbits by weighted reciprocal mass, uniformly over finite subfamilies; this uniform bound permits the passage to the infinite support. The short paper then chooses the modulus and block length so that its error charged to the whole weighted mass tends to zero. The Lean proof first makes the remaining tail weight small and uses a different block-length schedule. Both produce a positive displacement below 1/𝑣1/v; their parameter schedules should be read with their respective error bounds.

Lean proves this as divisibilityWeightedClaim in WeightedReturn.lean. The short paper gives a shorter proof and an explicit support with divergent reciprocal sum satisfying the criterion. The comparison is with Erdős’s earlier reciprocal-summable condition, which he stated for every integer base after proving the pairwise-coprime case. For 𝑃 ={2}P={2}, write 𝑎 =2𝑘𝑚a=2km with 𝑚m odd: the weighted summand is 1/[𝑚(𝑏2𝑘 −1)]1/[m(b2k−1)]. In the short paper’s example 𝐴⋆ ={2𝑘𝑚 :𝑘 ≥1,𝑚 odd ,𝑚 ≤22𝑘}A⋆={2km:k≥1,m odd ,m≤22k}, dyadic blocks show that the odd reciprocals in the 𝑘kth layer sum to between 2𝑘/42k/4 and 2𝑘2k.

The layer therefore contributes at least 1/41/4 to ∑𝑎∈𝐴⋆1/𝑎∑a∈A⋆1/a, but at most 21−𝑘21−k to the base-two weighted sum. The ordinary reciprocal sum diverges while the weighted sum converges. The theorem gives irrationality at every integer base for every infinite subset of 𝐴⋆A⋆. It does not cover full support, all odd exponents, or the full prime support; Tao–Teräväinen prove the latter at base two by another method. The #257 reader exercise tests how changing a layer cutoff alters this certificate, and why a failed weighted test is not a rationality result.

A second test shows why a prime set fitted separately to each finite prefix cannot certify the infinite hypothesis. The weighted-support transfer exercise gives the complementary fixed-host phenomenon: for any prescribed finite nonempty prime set, its binary weighted certificate can require every prime in that set. This is a calculation about the sufficient criterion, not a claim that each infinite subset needs the same witness or that the example has been formalised separately in Lean. The comparison identifies the added class and proof mechanism, but does not settle independent novelty or priority assessment.

See the short paper’s theorem, example and sources. One host realises any finite monotone witness rule, checked in Lean as finite_monotone_witness_rule_realised. Given a finite set EE of primes and a nonconstant upward-closed rule on its subsets, a finite union of prime-cofactor blocks has divergent reciprocal sum, its weighted test converges at every base exactly when the witness primes in EE satisfy the rule, and every infinite subset has irrational subseries at every integer base. For three primes, any two suffice and none is individually mandatory. The worked variants compare this host with a different required-prime construction.

The construction is AI-assisted and its novelty has not been independently assessed. At base two, the weighted condition can also be combined with the positive divisor-cover criterion: the long paper proves that a common finite averaging window makes both displacements small. Every infinite subset of their union then has irrational subseries at every integer base. Lean proves this as mixedSupportClaim in the same module. Neither theorem establishes the separately proposed hosts separating the two classes. Every infinite reciprocal-summable support satisfies it, yielding the coprimality-free extension stated by Erdős.

Full-support irrationality at every integer base is classical (Erdős 1948) and Lean-checked here, as are pairwise-coprime summable-reciprocal support and Lebesgue measure one for the base-2 achievement set. Irrationality for every infinite support and the 1/21/2 and 1/211/21 branches remain open. The weighted theorem is Lean-checked. The exact five-declaration PalomarCorpus/E257_01 entry, which includes divisibilityWeightedClaim, passed Palomar mechanical verification for source commit b85ed30805188eb4390a686b111294b24363418e. Palomar registered version 1 as PALOMAR-2026-09-25-000009 on 25 September 2026.

The immutable record binds that version to submission gid0ym5uu910, the pinned source, and the five selected declarations. Registration and mechanical verification cover the selected interface, not every claim in the paper or the unrestricted Erdős problem. Read the short paper, long record, and separate Comparator verification status.

Read the public result guide

Check the 189/388 example

This exact-rational calculation concerns one proposed member of the Mersenne achievement set. It does not test the weighted irrationality theorem above or settle the universal Problem 257.

From the mathematics repository root, run the exact-rational script with Python 3:

python3 research/experiments/sparse_interpolation/late_rejection.py

Saved output excerpt from that script (the page itself does not run a check):

target: 189/388
first_rejection: 17
tail_upper_bound: 196609/25769803776
remainder: 9291822600689/1217890317075045460
weight: 1/131071

At step 17, the exact inequality is tail upper bound < remainder < current weight. Earlier greedy choices are certified, so this particular rational cannot be represented as a subsum of 1/(2^n−1). The script also checks 577/388 and a separate finite factorial calculation. Read the explanation and limits.

Continue with a broader finite probe

python3 research/experiments/choices_contraction/rational_membership_probe.py --hosts all --q 12 --depth 10 --horizon 80

This second script reports excluded when it finds a finite certificate, finite representation when it reaches zero, or not excluded through depth 10 when neither occurs in this run. Survival at finite depth does not prove membership. Read its method and saved results.

Introduction

For a set 𝐴A of positive integers and a real number 𝑏 >1b>1, write

𝑋𝐴(𝑏)=∑𝑎∈𝐴1𝑏𝑎−1.XA(b)=∑a∈A1ba−1.

This series converges by comparison with a geometric series, since (𝑏𝑎 −1)−1 ≤𝑏1−𝑎/(𝑏 −1)(ba−1)−1≤b1−a/(b−1). Erdős proved irrationality for full support at integer bases [5], and later proved the same conclusion for pairwise coprime supports of finite reciprocal sum [7]. On that page he stated that the coprimality assumption could be removed, without giving the details. The question for arbitrary infinite support in base two is Problem #257:

Problem 1.1 (Erdős #257). Is 𝑋𝐴(2)XA(2) irrational for every infinite 𝐴 ⊆ℕ>0A⊆N>0?

We seek conditions inherited by every infinite subset of the support. The first replaces reciprocal summability by a divisibility-sensitive weight. For 𝑎 =2𝑘𝑚a=2km with 𝑚m odd, it uses 1/[𝑚(𝑏2𝑘 −1)]1/[m(b2k−1)] in place of 1/(2𝑘𝑚)1/(2km): a large power of 22 can compensate for many odd cofactors. More generally, fix a finite set 𝑃P of primes and write ℎ(𝑎) =∏𝑝∈𝑃𝑝𝑣𝑝(𝑎)h(a)=∏p∈Ppvp(a) for the 𝑃P-part of 𝑎a, where 𝑣𝑝(𝑎)vp(a) is the exponent of 𝑝p in 𝑎a. The prime powers may grow with 𝑎a, but the prime set is fixed.

Theorem 1.2 (a weighted condition on the support). Let 𝑏 ≥2b≥2 be an integer, let 𝐴 ⊆ℕ>0A⊆N>0 be infinite, and let 𝑃P be a finite nonempty set of primes. Set ℎ(𝑎) =∏𝑝∈𝑃𝑝𝑣𝑝(𝑎)h(a)=∏p∈Ppvp(a). If

𝑊𝑏,𝑃(𝐴):=∑𝑎∈𝐴ℎ(𝑎)𝑎(𝑏ℎ(𝑎)−1)<∞,(1)(1)Wb,P(A):=∑a∈Ah(a)a(bh(a)−1)<∞,

then 𝑋𝐴(𝑏)XA(b) is irrational. In particular, the base-two condition

∑𝑎∈𝐴ℎ(𝑎)𝑎(2ℎ(𝑎)−1)<∞(W)(W)∑a∈Ah(a)a(2h(a)−1)<∞

implies that 𝑋𝐴(𝑏)XA(b) is irrational for every integer 𝑏 ≥2b≥2. Both conclusions are hereditary under passage to infinite subsets.

Consider the support

𝐴⋆={2𝑘𝑚:𝑘≥1, 𝑚 odd, 𝑚≤22𝑘}.A⋆={2km:k≥1, m odd, m≤22k}.

For a fixed 𝑘k, the sum of 1/𝑚1/m over the odd cofactors is of order 2𝑘2k. Thus the corresponding terms contribute at least 1/41/4 to ∑𝑎∈𝐴⋆1/𝑎∑a∈A⋆1/a, but at most 21−𝑘21−k to (W). The calculation in Section 2 proves both bounds. Every infinite subset of 𝐴⋆A⋆ consequently gives an irrational value at every integer base. Since ℎ/(2ℎ −1) ≤1h/(2h−1)≤1, the same theorem also includes reciprocal-summable supports. Section A gives a direct proof of Erdős’s stated extension.

The second condition uses joint divisibility: it bounds fractional powers of divisor counts by positive divisor sums (Theorem 3.1). Neither condition implies the other, but they combine: every infinite subset of 𝐸 ∪𝑉E∪V has irrational sum when 𝐸E satisfies the base-two weighted condition and 𝑉V has a summable divisor cover (Theorem 4.1). Two irrational subseries could sum to a rational number, so we must control their errors at the same index. The separating constructions in Proposition 5.1 give such a union outside both individual classes (Corollary 5.2). These are sufficient conditions, not a characterisation of the supports in Problem 1.1.

The proofs compare a multiple of 𝑋𝐴(𝑏)XA(b) with an integer. For a positive integer 𝑁N, put

Δ𝑏,𝐴(𝑁)=∑𝑎∈𝐴𝑏𝑁mod𝑎−1𝑏𝑎−1=(𝑏𝑁−1)𝑋𝐴(𝑏)−𝐽𝑏,𝐴(𝑁),𝐽𝑏,𝐴(𝑁)=∑𝑎∈𝐴𝑎≤𝑁⌊𝑁/𝑎⌋∑𝑗=1𝑏𝑁−𝑗𝑎.(D)(D)Δb,A(N)=∑a∈AbNmoda−1ba−1=(bN−1)XA(b)−Jb,A(N),Jb,A(N)=∑a∈Aa≤N∑j=1⌊N/a⌋bN−ja.

Division of 𝑁N by each 𝑎a gives the identity. At an integer base, 𝐽𝑏,𝐴(𝑁)Jb,A(N) is an integer; for infinite 𝐴A, the displacement is positive because some 𝑎 ∈𝐴a∈A exceeds 𝑁N. Thus, if 𝑋𝐴(𝑏) =𝑝/𝑞XA(b)=p/q with 𝑝 ∈ℤp∈Z and 𝑞 ≥1q≥1 an integer, then 𝑞Δ𝑏,𝐴(𝑁)qΔb,A(N) is a positive integer and Δ𝑏,𝐴(𝑁) ≥1/𝑞Δb,A(N)≥1/q. We seek displacements tending to zero; Δ𝑏,𝐴(𝑁)Δb,A(N) itself is not a fractional part and may exceed 11. Erdős also proposed using fractional parts of powers times the series value [7].

Divisibility cancels finitely many exponents when 𝑁N is a multiple of their least common multiple. The remaining terms have small complete-period means when their gcd with the modulus is large. Incomplete-period bounds lack a factor 1/𝑎1/a. Averaging over dyadic lengths restores it: an exponent enters the truncated error only when the sampled range reaches it, and the reciprocals of subsequent lengths form a geometric tail bounded by a multiple of 1/𝑎1/a. Exponents beyond the sampled range are estimated separately. Explicit modulus dependence lets both criteria share this average.

Sections 2–4 prove the three criteria; Sections 5–6 separate their support classes and explain the method’s limits. The appendices give the direct reciprocal-summable proof, finite-denominator results and rational-membership tests. The last of these decide neither 1/21/2 nor 1/211/21.

Finite averages and the weighted criterion

Fix the integer base 𝑏b and the finite prime set 𝑃P. We first estimate averages over multiples of a fixed modulus 𝑄Q, then choose 𝑄Q to exploit the weighted hypothesis. The role of the gcd is already visible at 𝑏 =2b=2, 𝑄 =4Q=4 and 𝑎 =6a=6: the residues are 4,2,04,2,0, and

13(24−163+22−163+0)=221≤26(22−1)=19.13(24−163+22−163+0)=221≤26(22−1)=19.

Duverney–Tachiya [1] also bound an average on an arithmetic progression and select an index controlling a combined quantity. Their progression is built by the Chinese remainder theorem. Here the additional dyadic average controls the incomplete-period error as the modulus grows.

An example beyond reciprocal summability

For the support in the introduction, the two sums can be compared layer by layer. Recall that

𝐴⋆={2𝑘𝑚:𝑘≥1, 𝑚 odd, 𝑚≤22𝑘}.A⋆={2km:k≥1, m odd, m≤22k}.

The layers are disjoint, since their elements have different 22-adic valuations. For 𝑟 ≥2r≥2, put

𝑆𝑟=∑𝑚≤2𝑟𝑚 odd1𝑚.Sr=∑m≤2rm odd1m.

The weighted criterion treats exponents separately. A divisor cover instead uses their joint divisibility. To describe it, write the series in terms of its divisor counts:

Membership requires one finite prime set or one summable cover for the whole support. The constructions below exclude every such choice.

Proposition 5.1 (incomparable support criteria). There are infinite positive supports 𝐸E and 𝑉V such that

𝐸∈W2,𝐸∉C,𝑉∈C,𝑉∉W𝑏 (𝑏≥2),∑𝑎∈𝑉1𝑎=∞.E∈W2,E∉C,V∈C,V∉Wb (b≥2),∑a∈V1a=∞.

Both constructions use {𝑞𝑑 :𝑑 ∣∏𝑝∈𝑃𝑝}{qd:d∣∏p∈Pp}, with opposite divisibility patterns. For 𝐸E, growing powers 𝑞 =2𝑘q=2k make the weighted sum converge, while simultaneous divisors obstruct every cover. For 𝑉V, disjoint prime sets force every finite-prime weighted sum to diverge, while fractional powers of the divisor counts make the cover cost summable.

A strict enlargement and finite unions

The mixed theorem now applies to a support outside both individual classes.

Corollary 5.2 (a support requiring the mixed criterion). There is an infinite positive support 𝑈U with 𝑈 ∉CU∉C and 𝑈 ∉W𝑏U∉Wb for every integer 𝑏 ≥2b≥2, such that 𝑋𝐴(𝑏)XA(b) is irrational for every infinite 𝐴 ⊆𝑈A⊆U and every integer 𝑏 ≥2b≥2.

Proof. Let 𝑈 =𝐸 ∪𝑉U=E∪V, with 𝐸,𝑉E,V as in Proposition 5.1. A cover of 𝑈U is also a cover of 𝐸E, while convergence of the weighted sum over 𝑈U would imply convergence of the sum over 𝑉V for the same prime set, since all summands are nonnegative. Thus 𝑈U belongs to neither individual class. Theorem 4.1 gives irrationality for every infinite subset of 𝑈U at every integer base 𝑏 ≥2b≥2. ◻

The fixed-dyadic cover class in (V) is closed under finite unions. When interleaving two covers, we must control the index-dependent factor 2𝑗𝛼𝑗2jαj. Place their 𝑗jth finite sets at positions 2𝑗 −1,2𝑗2j−1,2j and halve each exponent; this factor then does not increase. The old majorant coefficients still work, since 𝑓𝛼/2 ≤𝑓𝛼fα/2≤fα for every nonnegative integer 𝑓f. It remains to compare the denominators in the cost. Writing 𝑇𝑗 =𝐶𝑗2𝑗𝛼𝑗/(2𝛼𝑗 −1)Tj=Cj2jαj/(2αj−1) for the original 𝑗jth cost, its new cost is at most

𝐶𝑗2𝑗𝛼𝑗2𝛼𝑗/2−1=(1+2𝛼𝑗/2)𝑇𝑗≤(1+√2)𝑇𝑗.Cj2jαj2αj/2−1=(1+2αj/2)Tj≤(1+2)Tj.

For 𝑟r covers, interleave at positions at most 𝑟𝑗rj and divide each exponent by 𝑟r; the cost ratio is (2𝛼 −1)/(2𝛼/𝑟 −1) <2𝑟(2α−1)/(2α/r−1)<2r. Weighted supports are also closed under finite unions: take the union of their prime sets: ℎ𝑃(𝑎)hP(a) can only increase, and ℎ/(𝑏ℎ −1)h/(bh−1) decreases with ℎh. Both criteria are hereditary and admit finite supports. Their mixed class is therefore closed under finite unions and finite changes, already with the fixed dyadic weights in (V). Countable unions need not remain in the mixed class: every prime singleton is admitted, but full prime support fails the small-displacement condition, as shown in Section 6. The reciprocal-summable class is contained in the weighted class, since ℎ/(2ℎ −1) ≤1h/(2h−1)≤1. A direct proof appears in Appendix A.

Limits of the small-displacement criterion

Small displacement is a sufficient condition for irrationality, not a necessary one. Full support already shows the distinction:

Δ2,ℕ>0(𝑁)>(2𝑁−1)∑𝑎>𝑁2−𝑎=1−2−𝑁≥12(𝑁≥1).Δ2,N>0(N)>(2N−1)∑a>N2−a=1−2−N≥12(N≥1).

The full-support value is nevertheless irrational [5]. Thus a proof for arbitrary support cannot rely on making these displacements tend to zero in every case. Other uses of the displacement, integer linear forms and averaging arguments are not excluded.

Full prime support gives a second obstruction. Although every prime singleton is admitted by both support criteria, for the set of all primes PP one has Δ2,P(𝑁) >1/3Δ2,P(N)>1/3 for every 𝑁 ≥1N≥1: indeed ∑𝑟≥12−𝑟𝜔(𝑁 +𝑟) ≥1∑r≥12−rω(N+r)≥1, whereas 𝑋P(2) ≤∑𝑎≥2(2𝑎 −1)−1 <2/3XP(2)≤∑a≥2(2a−1)−1<2/3. Here 𝜔(𝑛)ω(n) is the number of distinct prime divisors of 𝑛n.

Yet Tao–Teräväinen prove the full-prime case at base 22 [3]. The paragraph following it states extensions to prime support at every integer base and to full prime-power support at base 22, leaving the modifications to the reader. It does not treat arbitrary infinite thinnings. The proposed thinning extension is not a premise of any theorem here.

The logarithmic lower bound is not a converse: replacing a fractional majorant by a logarithmic one need not control averages along the multiples of a prescribed modulus. The counterexample and the bound that remains valid on ordinary initial intervals are proved in Section 13 of the companion paper; those proofs were first worked out in an AI-assisted note of 17 September 2026. These are statements about finite averages; they do not rule out an irrationality criterion based on other uses of logarithmic divisor counts.

For squarefree support, Duverney and Tachiya’s theorem already gives irrationality. It holds at every base 2𝑗2j, 𝑗 ≥1j≥1, by Corollary 1.2 and Example 1.1 of Duverney and Tachiya [1]. Their corollary covers the 𝑠s-free products of any pairwise coprime sequence of polynomial growth, and they present it as support for the conjecture of Erdős and Graham stated here as Problem 1.1. For the squarefree support with 11 removed, the divisor count is 2𝜔(𝑛) −12ω(n)−1, which is odd for 𝑛 ≥2n≥2. This excludes a first-block-divisibility condition at even bases. Adjoining 11 removes that parity obstruction while changing the sum by a rational number. The argument concerns that normalisation of the certificate, and gives no obstruction to irrationality of the sum. Details and the other known support families appear in the comparison with known support theorems in the companion paper.

A growth-only criterion gives a different class: if 𝐴 ={𝑐1 <𝑐2 <⋯}A={c1<c2<⋯} and lim sup𝑛𝑐𝑛/2𝑛 =∞lim supncn/2n=∞, then 𝑋𝐴(𝑏)XA(b) is irrational for every integer 𝑏 ≥2b≥2 [8]. The same section of the companion paper proves the translation from denominator growth and gives examples showing that this class and reciprocal summability are incomparable. The interval-filling constructions in [9] and the freely chosen lacunary denominators of [16] are not constructions of subseries of these fixed Mersenne weights.

Prime-incidence arguments require additional care as well: multiplying all prime exponents by 22 creates positive correlations between their divisibility indicators. The identity and covariance calculation appear at the end of the companion paper’s discussion of mixed supports. Size conditions alone do not supply that independence.

Algebraic bases on separated supports

The companion Reading eight Erdős problems together, subsection “Divisibility cuts at every algebraic base”, states a transcendence extension based on the number-field Subspace Theorem. Its hypothesis is an infinite set 𝐻H with indices 𝐿𝑗 <𝑀𝑗Lj<Mj, where 𝐿𝑗 →∞Lj→∞ and 𝑀𝑗 −𝐿𝑗 →∞Mj−Lj→∞, such that every 𝑛 ∈𝐻n∈H with 𝑛 ≤𝐿𝑗n≤Lj divides 𝐿𝑗Lj, and every 𝑛 ∈𝐻n∈H with 𝑛 >𝐿𝑗n>Lj is a multiple of 𝑀𝑗Mj. The claimed conclusion is transcendence of ∑𝑛∈𝐵𝑤𝑛/(𝑡𝑛 −1)∑n∈Bwn/(tn−1) for every infinite 𝐵 ⊆𝐻B⊆H, bounded positive integer weights 𝑤𝑛wn and real algebraic 𝑡 >1t>1.

Every divisibility chain has such cuts, as does 𝐻∗ =⋃𝑗𝑁𝑗{1,…,2𝑁𝑗}H∗=⋃jNj{1,…,2Nj} with 𝑁0 =1N0=1 and 𝑁𝑗+1 =2𝑁𝑗lcm⁡(1,…,2𝑁𝑗)Nj+1=2Njlcm⁡(1,…,2Nj). Each block has a reciprocal sum of at least 1/21/2 and contains antichains of unbounded size. The weighted sum for one prime is at most 2𝑡2/(𝑡 −1)32t2/(t−1)3 at every real 𝑡 >1t>1. This connects the example with the weighted criterion, although the separation condition is not asserted for every support satisfying that criterion.

The companion proof is outside this paper and is not a premise of the weighted, cover or mixed theorem. It has two AI proof reviews, no Lean proof of transcendence and no independent human review. No historical priority is asserted for the extension. The case of arbitrary infinite support at base two remains unresolved.

Reciprocal-summable supports

Erdős stated the following extension of his pairwise-coprime theorem [7]. It follows from Theorem 1.2, since ℎ/(2ℎ −1) ≤1h/(2h−1)≤1, but the direct argument explains why reciprocal summability makes the averaging simpler.

Theorem A.1 (reciprocal-summable supports). Let 𝐴 ⊆ℕ>0A⊆N>0 be infinite. If

∑𝑎∈𝐴1𝑎<∞,∑a∈A1a<∞,

then 𝑋𝐴(𝑏)XA(b) is irrational for every integer 𝑏 ≥2b≥2.

Erdős also discussed weaker conditions [7]. We do not identify our weighted hypothesis with the conditions he suggested.

Reciprocal summability permits two successive limits: first the observation length grows with the modulus fixed, then the modulus grows until each fixed exponent divides it. The two interchanges use different summable bounds; neither requires a period for the infinite support.

Powerful integers (all prime exponents at least two) have the form 𝑢2𝑣3u2v3, so their reciprocal sum is at most 𝜁(2)𝜁(3)ζ(2)ζ(3). The theorem therefore applies to every infinite subset. For full perfect-power supports, compare Duverney–Tachiya [1] and Luca–Tachiya’s earlier linear-independence results [13].

Finite-support denominator periods

The least common multiple of the selected exponents survives cancellation as the multiplicative order of the base modulo the reduced denominator.

Theorem B.1 (the exact denominator period). Let 𝐹 ⊆ℕ>0F⊆N>0 be finite and nonempty, let 𝑏 ≥2b≥2 be an integer, and let 𝐷𝐹 >0DF>0 be the denominator of 𝑋𝐹(𝑏)XF(b) in lowest terms. Then 𝐷𝐹DF is coprime to 𝑏b, and

Put 𝐿 =lcm⁡(𝐹)L=lcm⁡(F). Clearing denominators gives 𝐷𝐹 ∣𝑏𝐿 −1DF∣bL−1, so the upper divisibility for the order is immediate. For the reverse, fix a divisibility-maximal 𝑛 ∈𝐹n∈F with 𝑛 ≥2n≥2 and choose a prime ℓ ∣Φ𝑛(𝑏)ℓ∣Φn(b). With 𝑒 =𝑣ℓ(𝑏𝑛 −1)e=vℓ(bn−1), the cyclotomic fact in Section E gives ordℓ𝑒⁡(𝑏) =𝑛ordℓe⁡(b)=n for the full prime power ℓ𝑒ℓe. Every other selected exponent 𝑚m has 𝑛 ∤𝑚n∤m, hence 𝑣ℓ(𝑏𝑚 −1) <𝑒vℓ(bm−1)<e. The 𝑛nth summand has uniquely smallest ℓℓ-adic valuation and cannot cancel. Thus ℓ𝑒 ∣𝐷𝐹ℓe∣DF and 𝑛 ∣ord𝐷𝐹⁡(𝑏)n∣ordDF⁡(b). Taking all maximal selected exponents proves the order statement; the size bound follows from ord𝐷𝐹⁡(𝑏) ∣𝜑(𝐷𝐹) <𝐷𝐹ordDF⁡(b)∣φ(DF)<DF when 𝐿 ≥2L≥2. The case 𝐹 ={1}F={1} has order one directly.

The unique-valuation argument also permits signs ±1±1 on the finite summands. This signed extension is not included in the formal statement. The distinction between primes and prime powers is visible in

𝑋{2,3}(2)=1021,𝑋{2,6}(2)=2263.X{2,3}(2)=1021,X{2,6}(2)=2263.

In both examples 22 has multiplicative order six modulo the denominator. The first combines orders two and three; the second retains the order-six prime power 99, although no prime divisor of 6363 has order six. The boundary 𝐹 ={1}F={1} at base two has 𝐷𝐹 =𝐿 =1DF=L=1. These lower denominator bounds give no upper height control for infinite partial sums and do not decide an infinite-support value. Van Assche instead constructs approximants for the full Lambert series and proves both nonvanishing and decay of the associated integer linear forms [14]. That approximation mechanism does not follow from denominator survival alone.

In particular, 1/211/21 is not a finite subseries sum. If it were, the order of 22 modulo 2121 would force every selected exponent to divide 66. The exponent 11 is excluded since its weight is 11. Any sum containing 22 or 33 exceeds 1/211/21, whereas the only nonzero remaining sum is 1/631/63, from the exponent 66. This will distinguish finite and infinite representations in the next appendix.

Rational membership

The preceding results start from a support and prove irrationality. We now fix a target and ask whether any support represents it. The first recurrence is a necessary condition on a rational value; the greedy recurrence later gives an exact membership criterion. Neither supplies the missing arithmetic information for 1/21/2 or 1/211/21.

The cited finite crossing lemmas give additional consequences under their alignment hypotheses: an earlier finite prefix cannot occur, and a real greedy exponent must be skipped (the missing-prefix consequence of an aligned crossing, the real greedy skip forced by that crossing).

Sources, verification and reproducibility

For Erdős’s reciprocal-summable extension and fractional-part argument, see pp. 222 and 226 of [7]. The periodic theorem [12] is also stated in Luca and Tachiya’s account [11], and Hornich’s strict-tail theorem is proved in Nitecki’s exposition [10]. These expositions are the sources used here for those two results; the original articles were not independently retrieved. The Formal Conjectures file [6] is statement-level prior art, not a proof dependency.

Formal bindings concern statements, not every printed argument. The mixed implication has a formal proof; a separate formal construction of a separating support 𝑉V uses finite sets of squarefree divisors. The 𝐴⋆A⋆ calculation, printed fresh-prime construction, Corollary 5.2, signed finite-denominator extension and Theorem D.1 have ordinary arguments here, without independent human review. The strictness corollary has no formal binding in the record. The companion paper locates the separate comparisons for its three logarithmic-sampling results. No historical priority is asserted for the support comparison.

Reproducing the weighted theorem.

The two declarations for Theorem 1.2 are in the public source at commit 91ca3405. That snapshot pins Lean 4.29.1 in lean-toolchain and its Mathlib revision in lake-manifest.json. From a complete checkout, with elan installed, build the two modules with:

lake exe cache get
python3 scripts/lean_fast_build.py --jobs 2 \
  ErdosProblems.Erdos257.PaperCompleteR8.WeightedReturn \
  ErdosProblems.Erdos257.PaperCompleteR8.WeightedHereditaryClaim

The cache download is optional. The modules contain divisibilityWeightedClaim and finitePrimeWeighted_fixedBase_hereditary, respectively; their precise statements and associated checks are linked above.

The supplementary declarations are collected in the companion paper’s final source section, grouped by support criteria, finite denominators, integer recurrences and achievement sets.

What is checked in Lean
  • Irrationality at every integer base for the classical full support, reciprocal-summable supports, and the finite-prime weighted supports in divisibilityWeightedClaim.
  • Every infinite subset of the union of a finite base-two weighted-mass host and a strengthened positive-cover host has irrational series at every integer base (mixedSupportClaim).
  • Unique Mersenne coding on every support; compactness and nowhere density; perfection for infinite support; finite-complement measure 2−|𝐹|2−|F|, otherwise zero.
What is not checked
  • Universal irrationality over all infinite supports, or the proposed rational values 1/21/2 and 1/211/21.
  • Fair-bit laws, finer singularity results, and periodic-stride dimensions.
  • Any bridge from geometric uniqueness or measure rigidity to arithmetic irrationality.
The formal record: 15 main results, 2 open obligations, 1 selected result module, Comparator review

Main results

Statements and boundaries are copied from the corpus record. Registry status: programme_only

mixed prior-art geometry and locally proved metric result; novelty unassessed family: achievement_set_geometry

The base-2 Mersenne achievement set has Lebesgue measure exactly one.

This does not decide whether every infinite-support sum is irrational.

Erdos249257.volume_mersenneAchievementSet
formalisation of an existing theorem family: known_irrational_supports

For every integer base 𝑏 ≥2b≥2, the full-support Erdos-Borwein series is irrational.

This is the classical full-support theorem, not universal Erdos #257.

Erdos249257.irrational_erdosSum_full_support
locally proved result; novelty unassessed family: finite_prime_weighted_support

For every base 𝑏 ≥2b≥2, an infinite positive support A with finite prime-weighted mass in base b has irrational support series; if a positive host H has finite prime-weighted mass in base 2, every infinite subset of H has irrational support series at every base 𝑏 ≥2b≥2.

The finite-prime weighted-summability premise is explicit in both clauses. This criterion does not cover every infinite support or settle universal Erdős #257; no novelty, priority, significance, or external human-review claim is made.

ErdosProblems.Erdos257.PaperCompleteR8.divisibilityWeightedClaim
locally proved result; novelty unassessed family: finite_prime_weighted_support

For every base 𝑏 ≥2b≥2, if a positive host H has finite prime-weighted mass in base b, every infinite subset A of H has irrational support series in the same base b.

This hereditary result retains the same-base weighted-summability hypothesis; it does not infer all-base irrationality from weighted mass at an arbitrary base, or settle universal Erdős #257.

ErdosProblems.Erdos257.PaperCompleteR8.finitePrimeWeighted_fixedBase_hereditary
formalisation of an existing theorem family: pairwise_coprime_support

For every integer base 𝑏 ≥2b≥2 and every infinite pairwise-coprime support A with summable reciprocal mass, the support-restricted Mersenne series is irrational.

This is the pairwise-coprime support theorem, not universal Erdos #257; the infinitude, pairwise-coprimality, and summable-reciprocal hypotheses remain explicit.

Erdos249257.irrational_erdosSupportSeries_pairwise_coprime
formalised here; novelty unassessed family: periodic_nonnegative_weight_irrationality

For every integer base 𝑏 ≥2b≥2 and every eventually-periodic nonnegative rational coefficient sequence γ with a positive value at a positive index in its periodic region, the series ∑𝑎𝛾(𝑎)/(𝑏𝑎 −1)∑aγ(a)/(ba−1) is irrational.

This is the nonnegative rational eventually-periodic coefficient theorem; its nonnegativity, eventual periodicity, and positive-tail hypotheses remain explicit, and the broader mixed-sign periodic theorem is not claimed.

Erdos249257.irrational_ratWeightSeries_eventuallyPeriodic
conditional reduction; novelty unassessed family: orthogonal_petal_sunflower_reduction

For every support A carrying the finite-core OrthogonalPetalBouquet structure and satisfying the exact uniform SunflowerForcedSlotTailSelection predicate, the base-2 support-restricted Mersenne series erdosSupportSeries 2 A is irrational.

This is a conditional reduction: the bouquet structure and uniform tail-selection predicate remain hypotheses; neither is constructed for arbitrary supports, so this does not add an unconditional Erdos #257 support family or solve the universal problem.

Erdos249257.SupportSunflowerDichotomy.irrational_erdosSupportSeries_of_orthogonalPetalBouquet
locally proved result; novelty unassessed family: finite_period_noncollapse

For a reduced finite Mersenne sum, the base order modulo the denominator equals the support lcm.

The finite-support theorem does not settle any infinite-support sum.

Erdos249257.finite_period_noncollapse_rat_den
locally proved result; novelty unassessed family: restricted_achievement_sets

A support-restricted Mersenne achievement set has exact finite-complement measure or measure zero for infinite complement.

The measure dichotomy does not classify rational points.

ErdosProblems.Erdos257.volume_supportedMersenneAchievementSet_dichotomy
conditional reduction family: shifted_odd_tail_state

A rational support value with a positive support seed and denominator 2𝑐 ∗𝑣2c∗v produces a positive natural shifted tail state with an exact binary recurrence and a modular doubling orbit modulo v.

This state-extraction theorem does not exclude rational infinite supports or settle universal Erdős #257; the support and rational-value hypotheses remain explicit.

Erdos249257.exists_shifted_odd_tail_nat_states_of_support_fraction
locally proved exact equivalence plus conditional consequences; novelty unassessed family: boolean_mobius_carry

For p : ℤ and 𝑞 >0q>0, a nonempty positive-index support with erdosSupportSeries 2 𝐴 =A= p/q exists exactly when a quotient-only Boolean–Möbius carry certificate exists, with positive square-root-bounded integer orbit, divisible carry differences, and support reconstructed from its Boolean Möbius transform.

The equivalence is stated at the existence level with 𝑞 >0q>0, 0 ∉ A, and a positive support witness; it gives no contradiction, no universal Erdős #257 irrationality result, and no producer of cofinally nonintegral shifts for the actual recurrence. The generic tempered-orbit theorem and the reciprocal-mass, unbounded-tail, and zero-window results are subordinate consequences, not separate families; the zero-window constant depends on the support and numerator and is not uniform. This does not settle every infinite support, and no novelty, priority, significance, external-review, or unrestricted #257 endpoint claim is made.

Erdos249257.exists_normalized_support_fraction_iff_exists_booleanMobiusCarry
conditional reduction; novelty unassessed family: boolean_mobius_exact_row_dynamics

If positive rational-greedy skips occur cofinally in the declared sense, the skipped-core construction supplies cofinally many exact local Mersenne half rows and hence (1 / 2 : ℝ) belongs to the Mersenne achievement set.

This route is conditional on the unproved CofinalPositiveHalfGreedySkips premise: for every N there is 𝑐 ≥maxc≥max N 4 with a positive greedy remainder below mersenneWeightRat c. A finite exact row or any finite collection of exact rows does not establish that cofinal supply. The result is a conditional 1/2-membership/counterexample route only, not an unconditional solution of Erdős #257; the exact-row, upper-half Boolean-word, rank-two, and endpoint-defect declarations are subordinate mechanism evidence, and no novelty, priority, significance, or external-review claim is made.

Erdos249257.half_mem_mersenneAchievementSet_of_positiveHalfGreedySkips
locally proved exact endpoint classification; novelty unassessed family: half_membership_seam_classification

Membership of 1/21/2 in the Mersenne achievement set is equivalent to unbounded false successor terminal bits, equivalently to an unbounded upper-or-middle successor branch, cofinal terminal-false positions, unbounded skipped ranks along the integer seam, infinite greedy skipped support, and no last half-greedy skip.

This exact endpoint-socket classification does not supply any unbounded terminal-false or upper-or-middle occurrences, cofinal supply, skipped-support producer, or half-membership witness; finite exact rows do not establish the required global supply. It is not an unconditional or universal Erdős #257 result, and no novelty, priority, significance, or external-review claim is made.

Erdos249257.half_mem_mersenneAchievementSet_iff_unboundedTerminalFalse
unconditional progress family: composite_dilation_defect_identity

For a positive support element a and positive x, the divisor-count coefficient at a*x splits into the coefficient at x, the distinguished new divisor when a does not divide x, and an exact finite composite-dilation defect.

The exact defect is not bounded for arbitrary supports and supplies no tail selector or irrationality theorem; the separate bouquet budget remains conditional on its structural hypotheses.

Erdos249257.CompositeDilationDefect.supportCoeff_mul_eq_add_defect
no-go result family: half_and_twenty_one_frontiers

For positive odd integers p, D, and q, the integer form of the two-thirds band forces 𝑝 ≥7p≥7; the small odd numerator classes 1, 3, and 5 are therefore excluded.

This is local 2-adic band arithmetic: 𝑝 =7p=7 is sharp for the stated hypotheses, and the theorem does not prove that an actual half-greedy orbit reaches or avoids the band, nor does it prove half-membership.
